Style: cinematic - realistic

A vintage, dull green Mini Cooper drives quickly past the camera on a dirt road. Two women are visible in the back seat, and one man is driving from the front. The car's headlights shine brightly as it passes, creating a blurred motion effect. The camera remains static, capturing the scene in a single, fixed frame with the sound of the engine roaring and tires crunching on the gravel.
chunk may not be needed if dynamic vram working and it all fits in, else use it but dont do more than 2 is Kijai recommendation - Mark, March 2026

# READ ME FIRST

**MAJOR CHANGE IN MY APPROACH WITH LTX-2.3 vrs LTX-2**:

March 2026. LTX 2.3 I find using audio in often doesnt work for lipsync and I dont know why. But a new approach works just as well.

- instead of creating the audio with Vibe Voice and using it here, I use timings in the prompt like below and let the LTX-2.3 model make the audio. LTX-2.3 has much better audio and timing capabilities, and doing this allows it to adapt the faces to what it wants rather than fighting it with forcing the audio-in. I leave this section here bypassed as it might be of use sometimes, but will be using prompt timings then swapping the dialogue out later. This "over-dubbing of sound" is fairly normal practise anyway in movies these days. Prompt example using timings:
</br>
	```
	a man with curly blond medium length hair is sat in a parked car.
	0-4 seconds he asks, "what are you two wandering about dressed like that for in this weather?"
	4-6 seconds he says, "You'll catch your death of cold."
	8-9 seconds he asks, "Can I give you a lift?"
	perfect natural lipsync and correct pronunciation.
	```
</br>

I'm working to 24 fps everywhere but LTX-2.3 audio is 25 fps strictly speaking. You may need to adjust everything to suit your chosen fps as it will effect your frame lengths. The had to be set manually here as "get node" doesnt work with this node. - Mark, March 2026

Cinematic Widescreen (2.39:1)

    1536 x 640 (Efficient Wide)

Square (1:1)

    768 x 768 (Fast)
    1024 x 1024 (Standard)

⚠️ Performance Note: Since you are rendering natively (no upscale), 1920x1088 uses significantly more VRAM than the default workflow. If you get OOM errors, reduce your Frame Count (Length) to roughly 49-65 frames.

# 1a IMAGE-TO-VIDEO STRUCTURE WORKFLOW

For more info - [MarkDKBerry.com](https://www.markdkberry.com)

Last update to notes - 3rd May 2026

current file name: `1a. MBEDIT-i2v_kj_LTX23_prompt_relay_vrsX.json`

---

This is adapted from what was originally `1a. MBEDIT-i2v_kj_LTX23_extend_audio-in_devQ5_vrs3.json` and shared as part of the `video-workflow-pipeline-180426.zip` batch of workflows.

Because I am now using it strictly for the first image-to-video stage to make 480 x 201 (or 16:9 equivalent), I have made some changes relevant to that purpose, so I am now cleaning it up a bit. 

If you want the old workflow see the notes above. If you are following my process then keep with this and the updates I provide for it.

# WHAT I USE THIS WORKFLOW FOR

Tweaking image to video prompts and getting first video structure of the shot from final base images.

I make 480 x 201 quick structural video clips, no audio, and then use the result when I am happy to run it through the v2v upscaler workflows to get it to 1080p (1920 x whatever in reality).

I am on LowVRAM and that is why I split tasks into their own workflows like this.



---

# MODELS AND LORAS

currently I am using LTX 2.3 Dev Q5KM GGUF model with distilled lora. That is the backbone.

I also use the VBVR reasoning lora to help structure, and update it as new ones get released.  [https://huggingface.co/LiconStudio/Ltx2.3-VBVR-lora-I2V/discussions/1](https://huggingface.co/LiconStudio/Ltx2.3-VBVR-lora-I2V/discussions/1) in that link is the civitai V3 version made by someone else which also seemed pretty good but I tend to use Licon version.

for this step its all I need.

---

# AUDIO / LIPSYNC

I am not using audio at all at this stage but left the audio loading and audio creation part in for you if you want to use it. 

- It's currently unplugged at the video combine output node so plug that back in if you want audio.

---

# NEW THINGS & CHANGES

- **I removed the extensions as I never use them** but if you need them either copy the first box over or revisit the original workflow and copy them in. I dont see the point since I wont be extending here so its just clutter.</br>

- **changed from manual sigmas to use ClownScheduler from RES4LYF** as it gives me more control over steps (sigmas) I use the linear quadratic setting as the arc is best for this structural stage. [github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF](github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF) </br>

- **Prompt Relay**. GET THIS!!!!!  I am using it here only to fix difficult shots, but its pretty good. Otherwise I set it to use the usual prompt. [https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-PromptRelay](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-PromptRelay)
   - currently NAG needs to be disabled when using Prompt Relay else you get an error.
   - I'll do a video on how I use it once I am more certain of its processing, so check my [YT Channel @markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry) for that.

NOTE: 24fps with 241 frames is 10 seconds.

(I may switch to 25fps in the future, I probably should since I think audio is at 25fps but I need more of a reason since it works. higher fps is higher frame count is longer time to finish).
